proof_method.worker_identity: log::Log callback at exact real mdns service_daemon.rs exec_command trace line 4058 calls the genuine Win32 GetCurrentThreadId. No product or worker source instrumentation, thread enumeration assumption, fabricated metric, private-field access or injected command.

proof_method.thread_inventory: Separate PowerShell observer refreshes the same live process identity and uses native System.Diagnostics.Process.Threads; requires nonempty thread inventory before and after cleanup.
proof_method.socket_inventory: Separate native observer uses GetExtendedUdpTable for AF_INET and AF_INET6, UDP_TABLE_OWNER_PID. Native data query must return 0; global combined inventory must be nonempty. Own PID filtering happens only after successful global queries. Size-query 122 is expected and recorded; malformed tables or exhausted resize retries throw.
proof_method.alive_proof: Each resource snapshot checks the helper process identity alive before and after OS queries. After worker and all owned UDP endpoints disappear, the observer receives a fresh ALIVE ping and takes another absence snapshot before sending exit.
proof_method.submission_is_not_acceptance: CLEANUP_RETURNED and public shutdown success are only boundaries. Neither acknowledgement, submission nor process exit supplies the cleanup verdict.
proof_method.baseline: Fresh helper READY snapshot occurs before any Discovery::new or network warm-up. Both cases: one main thread/zero UDP, then main plus log-bound mDNS worker/three UDP, then main only/zero UDP while alive. No additional persistent framework/runtime thread appeared in the recorded snapshots. Short-lived threads between snapshots are not excluded.
proof_method.explicit_shutdown_isolated_from_drop: The helper keeps Some(Discovery) after shutdown and through post-cleanup ping/snapshot. Drop happens only on later normal process exit, after the gate is already observed.
